chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, and from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I am your ransom, a man marries a woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah) for a month, then she becomes dear to him, and he wishes for his condition to be more than a month. Is it permissible for him to increase her wage and add to the days before the days he stipulated for her expire?' He said: 'It is not permissible; two conditions cannot be in one condition.' I said: 'What should he do?' He said: 'He should give charity to her for the remaining days, then he initiates a new condition.'
As for the child, he is attached to him in all cases.

key_terms.شَرْطَانِ فِي شَرْطٍ: Two conditions in one condition (legal principle)

ai.seo_question: How does a man extend the duration of a temporary marriage contract according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the mechanism of extending temporary marriage (*mut'ah*) by prohibiting dual conditions within a single contract, requiring the husband to compensate the wife for the remaining days via charity before initiating a fresh agreement. It underscores the jurisprudential principle of *shartan fi shart* (two conditions in one condition) while affirming the legitimacy of offspring, thereby ensuring clear lineage (*nasab*) within the flexible framework of Shia marital law.
